question: Why does a single-variant GWAS have almost no power for rare variants?

answers.answer: Each rare variant is carried by very few people, so there is not enough information at any one site to reach significance
answers.feedback: Correct — which is why the variants in a gene are tested together.

answers.answer: Rare variants are not genotyped accurately
Rare variants have no effect on traits

answers.feedback: It is not lower, and that is not the issue.

question: A gene-based test needs an annotation file, a set list and a mask. What does the mask decide?

answers.answer: Which functional classes of variant are included in a test — for example only predicted loss-of-function, or also missense

question: A burden test sums the rare variants in a gene. What does it assume, and when does that fail?

answers.answer: That they all act in the same direction; it loses power when a gene contains both damaging and protective variants
answers.feedback: Correct — this is why SKAT exists.

question: SKAT is a variance-component test and ACAT combines p-values. When is ACAT the better choice?

answers.answer: When you want to combine evidence across different tests or variant sets without assuming a single model
answers.feedback: Correct — ACAT is robust and cheap to compute.

answers.answer: When all variants act in the same direction
When the sample size is very small

question: The null model here is fitted with approximate Firth correction, which the quantitative-trait version did not use. What is it for?

answers.answer: Case/control imbalance — with few cases and rare variants, standard logistic regression gives badly inflated p-values
answers.feedback: Correct, and it is why binary traits need different handling.
That is what the LOCO predictions do.

question: regenie runs in two steps. What does step 1 produce?

answers.answer: A null model with per-chromosome (LOCO) predictions of the trait, which step 2 then conditions on
answers.feedback: Correct — leaving out the chromosome being tested avoids proximal contamination.
